title: Dysmenorrhoea - SREESURYA AYURVEDA
main_content:
Dysmenorrhoea
Dysmenorrhoea refers to painful menstruation characterized by recurrent cramps during the menstrual cycle, tiredness, abdominal discomfort, nausea, vomiting, and pain radiating to the thighs and calves from the lower back. Other symptoms may include pelvic ache and muscle soreness.

Causes
Primary dysmenorrhea is caused by uterine muscle contractions stimulated by prostaglandins. Secondary dysmenorrhea can be caused by conditions such as uterine fibroids, endometriosis, adenomyosis, polycystic ovarian syndrome, certain intrauterine devices (IUDs), medications, cancer, and pelvic inflammation.

Treatments
Ayurveda correlates dysmenorrhea to 'kashartava kashta,' meaning difficult menstruation. It is considered a 'vata pradhana tridoshaja vyadhi,' or a disease that involves all three doshas with a predominance in vata. Vata is the main cause of pain, aches, and cramps. The obstruction of apana vayu and arthavavaha srotas is the main cause of kashartava. Ayurveda offers a complete cure for dysmenorrhea through a proper diet, regimen, internal medication, and therapies.

Treatment Methods
- Internal medications
- Therapeutic treatments
- Yoga therapy

title: Diarrhea - SREESURYA AYURVEDA
main_content:
Diarrhea
Loose motions refer to the passing of loose and fluid consistency of feces that may or may not be recurrent over a period of time. This fluid consistency is sometimes associated with pus or bloody discharge. In Ayurveda, diarrhea is correlated to Atisara, where 'Ati' means large quantity and 'Sara' means fluid consistency.

Symptoms
- Bloated tummy
- Feeling nausea (vomiting sensation)
- Stomach cramps
- May be associated with pus or blood
- Loss of weight
- Loss of appetite
- Feeling uneasy
- High temperature

Treatments
Treatment is prescribed according to the involvement of the doshas (Vata, Pitta, and Kapha) and the strength of the patient. The physician may recommend:
- Internal medications with specific formulations
- Pathyas (dietary guidelines)

- Internal medications for pacifying Pitta and ama
- Diet and lifestyle modifications
- Therapeutic treatments like lepanam and swedanam

title: Hair Loss - SREESURYA AYURVEDA
main_content:
Hair Loss

Reasons for Hair Loss:
- Drug side effects
- Symptoms of a medical illness
- Fungal infection of the scalp
- Hereditary pattern baldness
- Alopecia

Symptoms of Hair Loss:
- Gradual thinning on the top of the head: This is the most common type of hair loss affecting people as they age.
- Circular or patchy bald spots.
- Sudden loosening of hair: This can occur due to physical or emotional shock.
- Full body hair loss: This can result from medical treatments such as chemotherapy.
- Patches of scaling that spread over the scalp due to ringworm.

Treatments for Hair Loss:
The common causes of hair loss include lack of essential nutrients in the body, excessive chemicals applied to hair, unhealthy diet, hormonal imbalance, dandruff or other scalp disorders, and excess stress.
- Internal medications tailored to specific conditions.
- Diet and hair care recommendations.
- Therapeutic treatments such as dhara, oil massage, swedanam, and masks.

Calcaneal Spur
These spurs typically form due to repeated stress or pressure on the foot, resulting in the accumulation of calcium on the heel bone. Ayurveda attributes calcaneal spurs to an imbalance in the vata and kapha doshas. Factors such as poor digestion, improper footwear, excessive walking, and obesity are believed to exacerbate these doshas, culminating in the formation of spurs.

Symptoms
- Persistent heel pain.
- Inflammation at the bottom of the heel.
- Pain when walking or exercising without supportive shoes.
- Feeling of a small, bony bump on the bottom or back of your heel.

Treatments
- Internal medications to alleviate vata and kapha doshas.
- Strict diet and lifestyle changes.
- Exercises and yoga therapy.
- Therapeutic treatments like lepanam, dhara, abhyangam, bandaging, and swedanam.

title: Diabetes & Related Issues - SREESURYA AYURVEDA
main_content:
Diabetes & Related Issues
Insulin is a hormone that regulates blood glucose. Hyperglycemia, also called raised blood glucose, is a common effect of uncontrolled diabetes and over time leads to serious damage to many of the body's systems, especially the nerves and blood vessels.

Symptoms
- Feeling very thirsty
- Needing to urinate more often than usual
- Blurred vision
- Feeling tired
- Losing weight unintentionally

Treatments
Over time, diabetes can damage blood vessels in the heart, eyes, kidneys, and nerves. Therefore, the right treatment at the right time is recommended to manage the condition effectively for a longer period.

- Herbal infusions for pacifying the vitiated doshas
- Diet
- Yoga and meditation
- Therapeutic treatments like Abhyanga, Dhara, Swedana, Virechana, etc.

title: Post Menopausal Problems - SREESURYA AYURVEDA
main_content:
Post Menopausal Problems
During this stage, menopausal symptoms, such as hot flashes, get milder or may go away. People in post-menopause are at increased risk for osteoporosis and heart disease. Medication or healthy lifestyle changes may reduce the risk of these conditions.

Symptoms
- Hot flashes and night sweats
- Vaginal dryness and sexual discomfort
- Depression, mood swings, anxiety, irritability
- Changes in sex drive
- Insomnia
- Dry skin
- Weight changes
- Hair loss
- Urinary incontinence

Treatments
Menopause is a natural phenomenon that occurs at the age of 45-55 years. Various hormonal changes take place in the body during this phase of life, which results in the development of several signs and symptoms that may disturb routine activities. During reproductive years, women are protected by female hormones, namely estrogen and progesterone. With menopause, women enter an estrogen-deficit phase in their lives, which accelerates the aging process, resulting in greater vulnerability to psychosomatic problems. These diminished hormone levels lead to the various symptoms seen in the menopausal phase.

Treatment options include:
- Internal medications according to the dosha vitiation
- Vata samana and Kapha vardhaka line of treatment
- Diet
- Yoga and meditation
- Exercise
- Rasayana therapy
- Therapeutic treatments such as snehana, swedhana, shirodhara, vasya, pichu, lepanam, etc.

The condition of Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) is known as 'Grahani' in Ayurveda. According to Ayurveda, the Agni is responsible for breaking down food into energy and nutrition. When digestion is complete, the food passes into the next stage of digestion through various digestive organs. If a person is unable to digest food easily, it implies that their digestion is weak, or the fire element 'Agni' is weak. This weak and improper digestion can lead to the accumulation of toxins, and all major symptoms of IBS can result from these toxins (ama).

Symptoms
- Experiencing irregular bowel habits such as alternating diarrhea and constipation
- Improper digestion and undigested food particles passing in motion
- Constant urge for motion immediately after a meal
- Pain in the abdominal area
- Bloating and nausea
- Sensation of incomplete evacuation with an urge for motion
- Heartburn, chest pain, and dysphagia
- In some cases, patients may experience fatigue, irritability, headache, anxiety, depression, and even urologic dysfunction and gynecologic symptoms.

Treatments
- Internal medications for improving digestive fire (Agni)
- Shodhana (purification therapies)
- Samana (balancing treatments)
- Vatanulomana (treatment for vata imbalance)
- Pathyas (dietary recommendations)
- Therapeutic treatment

title: Rheumatoid Arthritis - SREESURYA AYURVEDA
main_content:
Rheumatoid Arthritis
Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disorder that affects various body systems, including the skin, eyes, lungs, heart, and blood vessels. It occurs when your immune system mistakenly attacks your own body's tissues. Unlike the wear and tear damage of osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis affects the lining of your joints, causing painful swelling that can eventually lead to bone erosion and joint deformity.

Symptoms
- Tender, warm, swollen joints
- Joint pain that lasts for six weeks or longer
- Joint stiffness that is usually worse in the mornings and after periods of inactivity
- Fatigue, fever, and loss of appetite
- Joint pain and tenderness
- Small joints (wrists, certain joints in the hands and feet) are typically affected first
- The same joints on both sides of the body are affected

Treatments
According to Ayurveda, rheumatoid arthritis (ama vata) is a condition characterized by the vitiation of vata dosha and the accumulation of ama in the joints. Shodhana and shamana treatments are advised in Ayurveda. The first and foremost line of management is Nidana parivarjana.

- Irregular menstruation and ovulation
- Multiple immature follicles
- Increased levels of male hormones
- Excess facial hair, hair thinning, and hair loss
- Acne, oily skin, or dark patches of skin
- Chronic pelvic pain
- Obesity or increased weight
- Diabetes and high blood pressure

Treatments

Ayurveda offers effective treatments for PCOD. These include herbal remedies, therapeutic treatments, and yoga therapy aimed at balancing hormonal irregularities and reducing Kapha and Vata doshas.

- Treatment for hormonal imbalance
- Medicines for menstrual irregularities, fat reduction, and hormonal issues
- Therapeutic treatments
- Diet and food plans
- Yoga therapy

title: Indigestion - SREESURYA AYURVEDA
main_content:
Indigestion
Gastroesophageal reflux disease and other conditions can lead to indigestion. According to Ayurveda, constipation is due to the imbalance in the vata dosha, which centers in the colon.

Symptoms
- Bloating
- Discomfort
- Feeling too full
- Nausea
- Gas

Treatments
According to Ayurveda, indigestion is known as Ajeerna. It can result from fasting or consuming food before the previous intake has been digested. Other causes include untimely food habits, heavy or dry food, psychological factors such as fear, anger, jealousy, suppression of natural urges, and excessive intake of water. A reduction in pitta activity with an excessive kapha characterizes the doshic profile of indigestion.

- Internal medications with herbal formulations are recommended.
- Strict advice for healthy food habits is essential.
- Pathyas (healthy dietary practices) should be followed.

title: Postnatal Care - SREESURYA AYURVEDA

headings.text: Pravasava Raksha at Sree Surya Ayurveda

main_content:
Postnatal Care
Postnatal care is essential for mothers after pregnancy, labor, and birth. It takes into account the individual needs and preferences of the woman. We provide comprehensive postnatal care aimed at enhancing the mother's wellness. This care helps the mother recover from labor exertion, balance vata dosha, reduce stretch marks, decrease belly size, and strengthen and cleanse the uterus.

Importance of Prasava Raksha
Ayurveda emphasizes the practice of prasava raksha, which rejuvenates the mind and body of the mother. After delivery, the vata dosha may increase, leading to back pain, abdominal pain, increased anxiety, and overall imbalance in the body. Specialized care, medications, and diet can help reduce vata dosha and assist the mother in regaining her physical and mental health. Prasava raksha should be practiced within the first three months following delivery, as this is a critical time for the mother to restore her physical and mental health and promote proper lactation. During this period, the uterus returns to its normal position, and all muscles, tendons, and ligaments related to the uterus regain their strength and elasticity.

Benefits of Postnatal Care
- Faster healing of the uterus and related organs.
- Strengthens and nourishes joints, muscles, and tissues.
- Improves the quantity of breast milk.
- Cleanses the uterus.
- Reduces back pain.
- Reduces mental stress and strain.

Prasava Raksha at Sree Surya Ayurveda
Our approach includes both external therapy and internal medications:
- Abhayanga (body massage with medicated oil)
- Kizhi
- Lepanam with herbal paste
- Herbal bath
- Dhoopanam
- Anjanam
- Bandaging the belly

In the case of cesarean sections, prasava raksha will commence only after 2-4 weeks, depending on the complete healing of the wounds.

Spondyloarthritis
The axial form affects mostly the pelvic joints and spine. The peripheral form affects the limbs.

Symptoms
Symptoms vary by type of spondyloarthritis:
- Pain, stiffness, and swelling in the lower back, hips, shoulders, knees, elbows, and areas where tendons and ligaments meet bone, especially after long periods of sitting or standing.
- Fever
- Fatigue
- Skin rash
- Inflammation in eyes or intestines

Treatments
According to Ayurveda, the involvement of vitiated vata and raktha causes spondyloarthritis (vatasonita).
- Ama pacahan (removal of toxins through herbal medication and therapies)
- Diet and exercises
- Improving the quality of lifestyle
- Therapeutic treatments such as abhyanga, swedana, lepana, etc.

- Yoga therapy and exercises
- Therapeutic treatments such as oil massage, nadi swetha, bandaging, and kizhi.

Ayurveda recommends a pitta-pacifying diet that includes cooling, alkaline foods and advises avoiding spicy or hot items. Lifestyle changes such as reducing exposure to heat and managing stress are crucial for treatment. Additionally, herbal formulations and pathyas (wholesome foods) may be suggested.

title: Psoriasis - SREESURYA AYURVEDA
main_content:
Psoriasis
Psoriasis in Ayurveda is a well-known skin problem referred to as 'kithibha'. It is an immune system affliction (auto-immune) that causes plaques, which are irritated or sore patches of thick, red, dry skin. Psoriasis can influence any part of the body, but the elbows, knees, and lower back are the most commonly affected regions. The scalp, nails, and palms may also be affected.

Symptoms
- Inflamed patches of skin
- Plaques on red patches
- Dry skin that might break and bleed
- Itching around patches
- Thick or hollowed nails
- Swollen joints
- Stress: Unusually high stress might trigger flare-ups
- Heavy alcohol consumption may also trigger flare-ups

Treatments
Ayurveda explains that impurities in the blood, connected with emotional aspects, are the reason for the disease. Psoriasis is said to occur due to the vitiation of vata and kapha. Treatments include:
- Herbal formulations
- Diet
- Yoga and meditation
- Therapeutic treatments according to the patient's condition
